chalkboard.title: What People Are Saying
bullets: The name mashes up CARE + LEAF — the bandage is even shaped like a leaf
It also echoes the English word 'leave,' as in wishing the wound goodbye — that double meaning is built into the name
Launched in 1997 after three years of development, when most Japanese bandages were still stiff PVC that didn't breathe
The fix: a high-density urethane nonwoven fabric that stretches both lengthwise and widthwise, so it flexes when you bend a finger
Reviews split — plenty say it stays put even when bent, but some warn that wearing it too long can stretch out your skin

usage_placeholder.description: 실제로 손가락 마디나 팔꿈치 같은 관절 부위에 반창고를 붙이고 굽혔다 펴면서 안 떨어지는 걸 보여주는 영상. 붙이는 손동작 클로즈업 + 구부리는 동작 반복이면 좋음. 10~15초 분량.

quotes.japanese: 粘着部分が伸びるから曲げても割と平気。粘着力も強くて剥がれにくいのに、剥がした後ベタベタしない！
quotes.translation: The adhesive stretches, so it's fine even when I bend it. It sticks strong and doesn't peel off easily, but it's not sticky at all once you take it off!

quotes.japanese: 曲がるところにつけてもつけやすいしよかったです
quotes.translation: Easy to apply even on joints that bend — I really liked it

quotes.japanese: 気をつけてほしいことがあって、めっぱこれいいけど、多分瞼伸びます。はい。すみません。
quotes.translation: One thing to watch out for — this works great, but if you wear it on your eyelid, it'll probably stretch the skin out. Yeah. Sorry about that.
